subject: physics

concepts.title: Point Object Approximation
concepts.definition: A simplification where an object is treated as a single mathematical point because its physical size is far less than the distance it shifts.
concepts.key_idea: Object dimensions are ignored when travel distance is significantly large.
question_patterns: can the body be considered a point object
identify if the object is point-like
when is the point object approximation valid

solution_steps.explain: evaluate the size of the object against the total path length

concepts.title: Instantaneous Velocity
concepts.definition: The specific rate of change of an object's position with respect to time at a particular moment.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, the tangent's slope to a position-time graph at any specific time.
question_patterns: find the instantaneous velocity
calculate the velocity at t = {t}
what is the rate of change of position

solution_steps.explain: determine the change in position over a tiny interval
velocity is the ratio of displacement to time

concepts.title: Average Acceleration
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, the total change in velocity of an object divided by the total time duration over which that change occurred.
concepts.key_idea: The slope of the line connecting two points on a velocity-time graph.
question_patterns: calculate the average acceleration
find the change in velocity per unit time
what is the acceleration over the interval

solution_steps.explain: subtract initial velocity from final velocity
subtract initial time from final time
acceleration is the rate of velocity change

concepts.title: First Equation of Motion
concepts.definition: A kinematic relation that determines the final velocity of an object based on its initial velocity, constant acceleration, and time elapsed.
concepts.key_idea: Velocity increases linearly with time under constant acceleration.
question_patterns: find the final velocity
calculate the speed after {t} seconds
how much velocity is gained

solution_steps.explain: multiply acceleration by the time elapsed
final velocity is the sum of starting speed and gain

concepts.title: Second Equation of Motion
concepts.definition: A kinematic relation that calculates the displacement of an object under constant acceleration over a specific time.
concepts.key_idea: Displacement is the distance's sum from initial speed and the distance from acceleration.
question_patterns: find the distance covered in {t} seconds
calculate the displacement
how far does the object travel

solution_steps.explain: multiply starting speed by time
half of acceleration times time squared
total displacement is the sum of both components

concepts.title: Third Equation of Motion
concepts.definition: A kinematic relation linking final velocity, initial velocity, acceleration, and displacement without requiring time.
concepts.key_idea: Relates the second power of speeds to the distance covered under constant acceleration.
question_patterns: find the final velocity given displacement
calculate the distance needed to reach speed {v}
what is the velocity after traveling {s} meters

solution_steps.explain: calculate u squared
multiply 2 by acceleration and displacement
final velocity is the root of the sum

concepts.title: Displacement from Velocity-Time Graph
concepts.definition: The geometric area enclosed between the velocity-time both curve and the time axis represents the total displacement.
concepts.key_idea: The integral of velocity over time provides the change in position.
question_patterns: find the displacement from the v-t graph
calculate the area under the velocity curve
what distance is represented by the graph area

solution_steps.explain: base time multiplied by initial velocity
half base times change in velocity
total area equals displacement

concepts.title: Free Fall Motion
concepts.definition: In brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, the motion of an object falling solely under the influence of gravity, with a constant downward acceleration.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, All objects in free fall experience the same acceleration regardless of mass.
question_patterns: calculate the height of free fall
find the time taken to hit the ground
what is the velocity of the falling object

solution_steps.explain: acceleration is -9.8 m/s^2
use second equation with zero initial velocity

concepts.title: Stopping Distance
concepts.definition: In brief, the distance a vehicle travels after brakes are indeed applied before it comes to a complete stop.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, Stopping distance scales with the initial's square velocity.

concepts.title: Reaction Time
concepts.definition: The time delay between an observer perceiving a stimulus and taking physical action.
concepts.key_idea: Can be measured by the distance a ruler falls before being caught.
question_patterns: estimate the reaction time
calculate how long it took to respond
find reaction time from fall distance

solution_steps.explain: numerator for the time equation
ratio of distance to acceleration
solve for time

concepts.title: Relative Velocity
concepts.definition: In brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, the velocity of one object as measured from the frame of reference of another moving object.
